concepts.learning_objective: State the Law of Conservation of Mass and verify it from given masses of reactants and products.
Explain why a reaction that releases a gas must be done in a closed system to show that mass is conserved.
State the Law of Constant (Definite) Proportions and use a fixed mass ratio to find unknown masses.
Explain why the law applies to compounds and not to mixtures.
Recall the postulates of Dalton's Atomic Theory.
Use Dalton's postulates to explain the laws of conservation of mass and constant proportions.

topics.title: Covalent bonding and naming covalent compounds

concepts.learning_objective: Define a molecule and a chemical bond, and explain why atoms combine to become stable.
Explain single, double and triple covalent bonds through sharing of electron pairs in molecules such as H2, Cl2, O2, HCl and H2O.
Name binary covalent compounds using the prefix system.

topics.title: Ionic bonding and naming ionic compounds

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how atoms form cations and anions by losing or gaining electrons.
Describe the ionic bond and the crystal structure of sodium chloride.
Name ionic compounds and recognise common monoatomic and polyatomic ions.
Write formulae of covalent and ionic compounds by criss-crossing valencies and reducing to the simplest ratio.
Write formulae containing polyatomic ions, using brackets where needed.

topics.title: Properties of ionic and covalent compounds

concepts.learning_objective: Compare the solubility of ionic and covalent compounds in water, kerosene and petrol.
Explain the electrical conductivity and melting points of ionic and covalent compounds.

topics.title: Molecular mass and formula unit mass

concepts.learning_objective: Calculate the molecular mass of a covalent compound from atomic masses.
Calculate the formula unit mass of an ionic compound and explain why ionic compounds have formula units.
